subject: science
cluster: The solar system and Earth's history
skillName: Plate Tectonics and the Age of Rocks

items.prompt:
The youngest ocean-floor rock is found
A) near the mid-ocean ridge
B) far from the ridge
C) on the Moon
D) only on land

steps: New floor forms at the ridge.

items.prompt:
When new ocean floor forms and spreads, it is called
A) seafloor spreading
B) erosion
C) evaporation
D) condensation

steps: New floor spreading is seafloor spreading.

items.prompt:
Earth's outer layer is broken into
A) plates
B) one solid piece
C) clouds
D) oceans only

steps: Earth's outer layer is broken into plates.

items.prompt:
As you move away from a mid-ocean ridge, the rock gets
A) older
B) younger
C) hotter only
D) softer

steps: Rock gets older farther from the ridge.

items.prompt:
New ocean floor forms when plates pull apart and
A) magma rises and hardens
B) water freezes
C) wind blows sand
D) nothing happens

steps: Rising magma hardens into new floor.

items.prompt:
Of two ocean-floor samples, the one farther from the ridge is
A) older
B) younger
C) the same age
D) not rock

The pattern of rock ages supports plate movement because
A) the ordered young-to-old pattern matches what spreading plates would make
B) rock ages are random
C) all rock is the same age
D) rocks do not move
items.answer: A) the ordered young-to-old pattern matches what spreading plates would make

steps: The pattern fits moving, spreading plates.

items.prompt:
The matched age pattern on both sides of a ridge is evidence that
A) the plates, and continents on them, move over time
B) continents never move
C) the ridge is shrinking
D) rock ages are fake
items.answer: A) the plates, and continents on them, move over time

steps: The pattern supports moving plates and continents.
